A proper reliability diagram requires probabilistic confidence estimates, which are absent here. Without these, standard scoring rules like the Brier score are inapplicable. The single validated metric—the spread-bucket gate—only measures marginal accuracy, not the full calibration of the system. This disconnect highlights a fundamental flaw: the model reasons about outcomes without generating well-calibrated uncertainty quantification, leading to overconfident or underconfident decisions.
